newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: HeShe expects to return to black.
newsitem.headline: HeShe expects to return to black.

text.p: Retailer and garment manufacturer HeShe Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to return to the black in the 1996/1997 financial year.
"With the Singapore problems contained, the group is likely to return to profitability this year," the company said after reporting its results for the year ended June 30, 1996.
Heshe has seven retail shops left in Singapore from 37 three years ago. It closed the outlets to stem its losses caused by the retail downturn and severe erosion of its competitiveness.
"Three more will be closed as the leases expire shortly," it said. The Singapore retail shop operation had been rationalised as part of its Malaysian operations to increase savings.
HeShe has also cut its factories in Singapore from four to one, but was studying new areas to try in the city-state.
The company said it had taken steps to relocate and develop businesses overseas, and entered the China market by acquiring the Fun group in 1994.

HeShe said its preparation for a separate listing of its North Asia division comprising operations in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan was progressing as planned. It added that it had started discussions for tie-ups and joint ventures.
